newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam slams U.S. sanctions against Burma.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam slams U.S. sanctions against Burma.

text.p: Vietnam said on Wednesday Washington's imposition of economic sanctions against Burma amounted to an interference in the internal affairs of a nation.

"As we have said clearly many times, Vietnam shares the view of many countries, considering that economic sanctions are imposed with the aim of interfering in the internal affairs of a nation..." the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
The ministry said economic sanctions were contrary to both the principles of equality and mutual benefit and the global trend in international relations.

Responding to a question on whether sanctions would affect Burma's entry into the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), the ministry said ASEAN had agreed in principle to admit Burma, Laos and Cambodia, and added: "...this is the internal affair of ASEAN".

The United States said on Tuesday it would ban new investment by American firms in Burma because of what Washington described as deepening political repression by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
The United States lifted a long-standing economic embargo on communist Vietnam in early 1994 and the two former enemies normalised relations in mid-1995.
